prompt: Find the slope of the line through $(1, 5)$ and $(5, 2)$. Write it as a fraction.
hint: Notice whether the $y$-values go up or down from the first point to the second. That decides the sign.

hints.text: Notice whether the $y$-values go up or down from the first point to the second. That decides the sign.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $(1, 5)$ and $(3, 1)$: rise $= 1 - 5 = -4$, run $= 3 - 1 = 2$, slope $= -2$. Same subtraction order every time.
The rise is $2 - 5 = -3$ and the run is $5 - 1 = 4$. Write rise over run and keep the negative sign.
Rise over run is $\frac{-3}{4}$, so the slope of the line is $-\frac{3}{4}$.

explanation: The rise is the change in $y$: $2 - 5 = -3$, negative because the line drops.
The run is the change in $x$, subtracted in the same order: $5 - 1 = 4$.
Slope is rise over run, so the slope is $-\frac{3}{4}$. The line goes down $3$ for every $4$ across.

alternativeExplanations.title: Subtract the other way
steps: Swap the order of BOTH subtractions: rise $5 - 2 = 3$, run $1 - 5 = -4$.
$\frac{3}{-4}$ is still $-\frac{3}{4}$ — same slope, as long as both are swapped together.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ Dodge the trap
steps: Flipping to run-over-rise gives −4/3 — right numbers, upside-down fraction.
Rise first, run second: (2 − 5) on top, (5 − 1) on the bottom → −3/4. Say “rise over run” as you write it.
